summary: Build supply chain resilience and business continuity skills with BIA, ISO 22301, supplier risk tools, and practical recovery planning.
lede: Continuity planning across supply networks helps organizations identify critical dependencies and prepare for disruption. For supply chain, procurement, operations, logistics, and business continuity professionals, the course offers practical ways to assess supplier risk, rank critical services, and plan recovery actions. Exercises cover business impact analysis, dependency mapping, continuity strategies, supplier escalation plans, and operational recovery playbooks.
audienceIntro: This course is built for you if you work where supply chain decisions meet continuity risk, supplier performance, and operational recovery. It speaks directly to roles that need practical tools for planning, response, assurance, and reporting across the supply network. Supply Chain Managers who own resilience priorities across suppliers and lanes. Procurement Managers who embed continuity clauses into supplier contracts. Operations Planners who manage recovery sequencing for critical workflows. Logistics Coordinators who reroute freight and alternate fulfilment paths. Business Continuity Managers who align ISO 22301 controls with operations. Supply Chain Risk Analysts who score supplier and network exposure. Inventory Planning Managers who design buffering and recovery stock policies. Crisis Management Leads who coordinate escalation and command decisions. Third-Party Risk Specialists who assess supplier continuity assurance. Operations Directors who brief executives on continuity readiness and recovery gaps.
prerequisites: Bring a laptop, a spreadsheet tool, and a real or realistic supply chain case from your organization if available. You should be ready to work with supplier lists, process maps, service level data, and continuity templates during the exercises.
